resources.string: Off by default. Sends displayed chat text to TypeSafe Jev and shows analysis below the matching bubble; requires an API key.

Save your key and settings here, then enable the switch. By default, entering a chat analyzes its latest configured number of messages. Enable render mode to analyze messages as they appear while scrolling; messages that scroll off-screen before processing are skipped. Each request sends TypeSafe up to the configured number of messages from the current conversation (a gap of more than 6 hours starts a new one), the quoted message, up to 3 later replies, and the chat background and extra context you wrote. Nearby messages are cut to 300 characters and older ones to 80; images, stickers and similar messages are sent as type placeholders only. Messages are analyzed again when more replies arrive. Results are cached in memory only; tap the label under a bubble to see details and set the background for that chat. More context takes longer and costs more; concurrent requests are limited separately. Reopen the chat after changing modes. Settings stay local.
Analyze text messages as they appear while scrolling
Most context messages sent with each request (cut at conversation gaps, 0–200)
Latest messages to analyze on chat entry (1–200)
Extra context sent with every analysis (for example: I speak bluntly); blank sends nothing
